problems.hint: Write the DP function and you only need to find the fix point.

legend: Billionaires Robin McBobin and Ronald Dump are playing the Game of Chance.

The game takes $$$n$$$ turns. On each turn, one of the players has the right of choice, Robin gets it for the first move. On each turn, an integer chosen uniformly and independently from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$ appears on the screen. The player with the right of choice has to choose whether to take this number and pass the right of choice to the opponent, or to give this number to the opponent but keep the right of choice for themselves.

Both Robin and Ronald are more interested in dominating their opponent than in gaining scores, so both will choose the option which would maximize the expected difference between their and the opponent's sum of numbers. Both players play optimally.

Let $$$d_n$$$ be the expected value of difference between Robin's sum and Ronald's sum after $$$n$$$ turns. It may be proven that for $$$m \geq 3$$$, there exists a rational number $$$d$$$ such that $$$\lim\limits_{n \to \infty} d_n = d$$$. You have to find this number.
input: The first line of input contains a single integer $$$t$$$ which is the number of test cases ($$$1 \leq t \leq 5 \cdot 10^5$$$).
Each test case is given on a single line containing a single integer $$$m$$$ ($$$3 \leq m \leq 10^9$$$).
output: For each test case, if $$$d=\tfrac{P}{Q}$$$ such that $$$P$$$ and $$$Q$$$ are coprime, output $$$(P \cdot Q^{-1}) \bmod (10^9 + 7)$$$. It is guaranteed that $$$Q \not\equiv 0 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$.
note: For $$$m=3$$$, the answer is $$$d=1$$$. For $$$m=4$$$, the answer is $$$d=1.333...=\tfrac{4}{3}$$$.

legend: 亿万富翁Robin McBobin和Ronald Dump正在玩机会游戏。
游戏分为 $$$n$$$ 回合。每回合，一位玩家拥有选择权，Robin 在第一步就获得了选择权。每回合，屏幕上都会出现一个从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$m$$$ 均匀且独立选择的整数。拥有选择权的玩家必须选择是否接受这个数字并将选择权传递给对手，还是将这个数字传递给对手但保留自己的选择权。
罗宾和罗纳德更感兴趣的是控制他们的对手，而不是获得分数，所以他们都会选择最大化他们和对手的数字总和之间的预期差异的选项。两名球员都以最佳状态比赛。
设$$$d_n$$$是罗宾的和与罗纳德的和在$$$n$$$转折后的差的期望值。可以证明，对于 $$$m \geq 3$$$，存在一个有理数 $$$d$$$，使得 $$$\lim\limits_{n \to \infty} d_n = d$$$。你必须找出这个数。
input: 输入的第一行包含一个整数$$$t$$$，它是测试用例的数量($$$1 \leq t \leq 5 \cdot 10^5$$$）。
每个测试用例在包含单个整数$$$m$$$($$$3 \leq m \leq 10^9$$$）的单行上给出。
output: 对于每个测试用例，如果$$$d=\tfrac{P}{Q}$$$使得$$$P$$$和$$$Q$$$互为共数，则输出$$$(P \cdot Q^{-1}) \bmod (10^9 + 7)$$$。保证$$$Q \not\equiv 0 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$。

problems.hint: Cases.

legend: There is a grid of $$$n \times n$$$ rooms. Rows are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ from top to bottom, and columns are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ from left to right. Room $$$(i,j)$$$ lies in row $$$i$$$ and column $$$j$$$.

There are $$$2n$$$ fans. For each row $$$i$$$, there is a row fan that cools every room in row $$$i$$$ when it is switched on. Switching on this fan costs $$$r_i$$$. For each column $$$j$$$, there is a column fan that cools every room in column $$$j$$$ when it is switched on. Switching on this fan costs $$$c_j$$$.
You may switch on any subset of the fans, paying the sum of their costs. A room is cooled if at least one of its row fan and its column fan is switched on.

Yazan starts in room $$$(1,1)$$$ and wants to reach room $$$(n,n)$$$. In one move, he may go to a room that shares a side with his current room. Every room in his path, including $$$(1,1)$$$ and $$$(n,n)$$$, must be cooled.
Find the minimum total cost of switching on fans so that such a path exists.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f486f19a17521299671fee85777ee738218601ce.png)
input: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^5$$$) — the number of rows and columns.
The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_n$$$ ($$$1 \le r_i \le 10^9$$$) — the costs of the row fans.
The third line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_n$$$ ($$$1 \le c_i \le 10^9$$$) — the costs of the column fans.
It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, output one integer — the minimum total cost required to create a cooled path from $$$(1,1)$$$ to $$$(n,n)$$$.
note: In the first sample, switching on the fan of row $$$1$$$ and the fan of column $$$3$$$ costs $$$1+1=2$$$. The diagram in the statement shows the cooled rooms and one possible path from $$$(1,1)$$$ to $$$(3,3)$$$.

legend: 有 $$$2n$$$ 风扇。对于每一行 $$$i$$$，当开启时，都有一个行风扇为 $$$i$$$ 行的每个房间制冷。开启这个风扇的费用为 $$$r_i$$$。对于每一列 $$$j$$$，当开启时，都有一个列风扇为 $$$j$$$ 列的每个房间制冷。开启此风扇的费用为 $$$c_j$$$。
你可以打开风扇的任何子集，支付他们的费用总和。如果一个房间的排风扇和列风扇至少有一个是打开的，那么这个房间就是在制冷。
Yazan 从 $$$(1,1)$$$ 房间开始，想要到达 $$$(n,n)$$$ 房间。一步之内，他可能会到达与当前房间共用一侧的房间。他路径上的每个房间，包括 $$$(1,1)$$$ 和 $$$(n,n)$$$，都必须进行冷却。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f486f19a17521299671fee85777ee738218601ce.png)
input: 第一行包含一个整数$$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$）——测试用例的数量。
每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$($$$2 \le n \le 10^5$$$)——行和列的数量。
每个测试用例的第二行包含 $$$n$$$ 整数 $$$r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_n$$$($$$1 \le r_i \le 10^9$$$)——行风扇的成本。
每个测试用例的第三行包含$$$n$$$个整数$$$c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_n$$$ ($$$1 \le c_i \le 10^9$$$）——列风扇的成本。
保证所有测试用例的 $$$n$$$ 之和不超过 $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$。
output: 对于每个测试用例，输出一个整数——创建从 $$$(1,1)$$$ 到 $$$(n,n)$$$ 的冷却路径所需的最小总成本。
note: 在第一个示例中，打开第$$$1$$$行风机和第$$$3$$$列风机的费用为$$$1+1=2$$$。声明中的图表显示了冷却室和从$$$(1,1)$$$到$$$(3,3)$$$的一条可能路径。

output: 对于输入$$$n$$$的每个测试用例，打印n行，每行有n个描述所需网格的整数。可以保证至少总是有一个解决方案。如果有多个答案，打印其中任何一个。

legend: Donghyun recently bought a square-shaped tablecloth. There are $$$N$$$ dots on the cloth, and the dots can be seen from both sides of the cloth. Donghyun thought that the tablecloth can be made more beautiful, so he decided to decorate the cloth with sewing.

For convenience, let's assume that each dot is a point on the $$$xy$$$-plane and the dots are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$N$$$. Dot $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le N$$$) is placed at coordinate $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$. No two dots have the same coordinates. A sewing sequence is an integer sequence $$$\{ s_i \}$$$ of length $$$k \geq 2$$$ satisfying $$$1 \le s_i \le N$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le k$$$) and $$$s_i \neq s_{i+1}$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le k-1$$$). The sequence draws edges on the cloth per the following rules:
Draw an edge connecting dot $$$s_{2i-1}$$$ and dot $$$s_{2i}$$$ on the front side of the cloth for all $$$1 \le i \le \left \lfloor \frac{k}{2} \right \rfloor$$$.
Draw an edge connecting dot $$$s_{2j}$$$ and dot $$$s_{2j+1}$$$ on the back side of the cloth for all $$$1 \le j \le \left \lfloor \frac{k-1}{2} \right\rfloor$$$.
Donghyun wants to make a beautiful pattern on the tablecloth, which is defined as the following:
For both sides of the cloth, all $$$N$$$ dots are connected by the edges on that side.
Two edges on the same side of the cloth can intersect only at a common endpoint.

Donghyun is very busy, so he wants to finish his sewing job as quickly as possible. In other words, over all sewing sequences that produces a beautiful pattern, Donghyun decides to choose the shortest such sequence. Your job is to find such a sequence.
Note that Donghyun wants to minimize the length of the sewing sequence itself, not the sum of the lengths of the edges he draws.
input: On the first line, a single integer $$$N$$$ is given. ($$$2 \le N \le 1\,000$$$)
For each of the next $$$N$$$ lines, two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ are given, which means dot $$$i$$$ is placed at coordinate $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$. ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le 10^9$$$)
No two dots are at the same coordinates.
output: On the first line, output a positive integer $$$k$$$, the length of the shortest sewing sequence that produces a beautiful pattern.
On the next line, output $$$s_1$$$, $$$s_2$$$, $$$\cdots$$$, $$$s_k$$$, the actual sewing sequence.
It can be proven that, for every possible input, there exists a sewing sequence that produces a beautiful pattern.
note: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8239e86f30641bde32ddc8c1c7182654ff24764b.png)
Figure 1. Visualization of sample output. Solid lines represent for edges on front side, dashed lines represent for back side.

legend: 东贤最近买了一块方形的桌布。布上有$$$N$$$个圆点，从布的两面都能看到。东贤认为桌布可以做得更漂亮，所以他决定用缝纫来装饰布料。

为方便起见，我们假设每个点都是 $$$xy$$$ 平面上的一个点，点的编号从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$N$$$。点 $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le N$$$）位于坐标 $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$。没有两个点的坐标相同。缝纫序列是长度为 $$$k \geq 2$$$ 的整数序列 $$$\{ s_i \}$$$ ，满足 $$$1 \le s_i \le N$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le k$$$）和 $$$s_i \neq s_{i+1}$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le k-1$$$）。该序列按以下规则在布上画边：
在布料正面为所有 $$$1 \le i \le \left \lfloor \frac{k}{2} \right \rfloor$$$ 绘制一条连接点 $$$s_{2i-1}$$$ 和点 $$$s_{2i}$$$ 的边。
在布的背面为所有的$$$1 \le j \le \left \lfloor \frac{k-1}{2} \right\rfloor$$$画一个连接点$$$s_{2j}$$$和点$$$s_{2j+1}$$$的边。
Donghyun 想在桌布上做出美丽的图案，其定义如下：
对于布料的两侧，所有 $$$N$$$ 点都通过该侧的边连接。
布料同一侧的两条边只能在公共端点处相交。
Donghyun 很忙，所以他想尽快完成缝纫工作。换句话说，在所有能做出漂亮图案的缝纫序列中，Donghyun 决定选择最短的序列。你的任务就是找出这样的序列。
请注意，Donghyun 想要最小化缝纫序列本身的长度，而不是他所画边缘长度的总和。
input: 在第一行中，给出了单个整数$$$N$$$。($$$2 \le N \le 1\,000$$$）
接下来的每一行 $$$N$$$ 都有两个整数 $$$x_i$$$ 和 $$$y_i$$$，这意味着点 $$$i$$$ 放在坐标 $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$ 上。($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le 10^9$$$)
没有两个点处于相同的坐标。
output: 在第一行，输出一个正整数 $$$k$$$，即能产生美丽图案的最短缝纫序列的长度。
可以证明，对于每个可能的输入，存在产生美丽图案的缝纫序列。
note: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8239e86f30641bde32ddc8c1c7182654ff24764b.png)
图 1. 样本输出的可视化。实线代表正面的边缘，虚线代表背面。

legend: Consider an undirected simple graph $$$G = (V, E)$$$. The problem of finding a node with similar connectivity is a well-researched topic, because it acts as a good metric to determine which nodes are relevant to other nodes. Services such as "friend recommendation" in Facebook is a good example of its applications. To formalize the notion of similarity, the concept of Jaccard similarity can be used, which is defined as $$$|N(v_1) \cap N(v_2)| / |N(v_1) \cup N(v_2)|$$$, where $$$N(v) = \{u | (u, v) \in E\}$$$.

Here, we will instead discuss the min-hashing method. Assume each node $$$v$$$ has the label $$$l_v$$$. The shingle value $$$s_v$$$ of node $$$v$$$ is defined as $$$s_v = \min \{l_u | u \in N(v) \}$$$. This method is efficient enough to keep up with industrial needs, and it is also a great metric for similarity: the Jaccard similarity between the set of neighbors $$$N(v_1)$$$ and $$$N(v_2)$$$ is an unbiased estimator of the probability that nodes $$$v_1$$$ and $$$v_2$$$ have the same shingle values, for random unique labels.

Let's think about a variant of min-hashing: we repeatedly perform min-hashing by taking the label as the previous iteration's shingle value. In this variant, for each node $$$v$$$ and the number of iterations $$$k$$$, the value $$$h^{(k)}_v$$$ is defined as
$$$$$$ h^{(k)}_v = \begin{cases} s_v, & \text{if $k = 1$}\\ \min \{h^{(k-1)}_u | u \in N(v) \}, & \text{if $k \geq 2$} \\ \end{cases} $$$$$$

For each $$$k$$$, let $$$c_k$$$ be the number of unordered pairs of distinct vertices $$$\{u, v\}$$$ such that $$$h^{(k)}_u = h^{(k)}_v$$$. Then, how does the value $$$c_k$$$ change as $$$k$$$ increases? In this problem, your task is to compute $$$\max_{k \in \mathbb{N}} c_k$$$.
input: The first line contains two positive integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ $$$(1 \leq n \leq 100\,000, 1 \leq m \leq 250\,000)$$$ representing the number of nodes and the number of edges, respectively. The nodes are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. Note that these are not the labels of the nodes.
The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers comprising a permutation of the first $$$n$$$ positive integers, where the $$$i$$$-th number in the line represents the initial label of node $$$i$$$.

Each of the next $$$m$$$ lines contains two integers. The $$$i$$$-th of these lines contains two distinct integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$ $$$(1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n)$$$, which means $$$\{u_i, v_i\} \in E$$$.
The input will be set in a way such that there are no self-loops, parallel edges, or nodes with a degree of zero.
output: Print the maximum value of $$$c_k$$$ over all positive integers $$$k$$$.

legend: 考虑一个无向简单图$$$G = (V, E)$$$。寻找具有相似连通性的节点的问题是一个研究得很好的主题，因为它可以作为确定哪些节点与其他节点相关的良好度量。Facebook上的“好友推荐”服务就是一个很好的例子。为了形式化相似性的概念，可以使用Jaccard相似性的概念，定义为$$$|N(v_1) \cap N(v_2)| / |N(v_1) \cup N(v_2)|$$$，其中$$$N(v) = \{u | (u, v) \in E\}$$$。

在此，我们将讨论最小哈希方法。假设每个节点 $$$v$$$ 都有标签 $$$l_v$$$。节点 $$$v$$$ 的分组值 $$$s_v$$$ 定义为 $$$s_v = \min \{l_u | u \in N(v) \}$$$。这种方法效率很高，足以满足工业需求，而且它也是一个很好的相似度度量：对于随机唯一标签来说，邻居集 $$$N(v_1)$$$ 和 $$$N(v_2)$$$ 之间的 Jaccard 相似度是节点 $$$v_1$$$ 和 $$$v_2$$$ 具有相同标记值的概率的无偏估计值。
让我们考虑一种最小哈希的变体：我们通过将标签作为上一次迭代的板块值来重复执行最小哈希。在这种变体中，对于每个节点 $$$v$$$ 和迭代次数 $$$k$$$，值 $$$h^{(k)}_v$$$ 被定义为
$$$$$$ h^{(k)}_v = \begin{cases} s_v, & \text{if $k = 1$}\\ \min \{h^{(k-1)}_u | u \in N(v) \}, & \text{if $k \geq 2$} \\ \end{cases} $$$$$$
对于每个$$$k$$$，让$$$c_k$$$是$$$h^{(k)}_u = h^{(k)}_v$$$的无序的不同顶点$$$\{u, v\}$$$对的数目。那么，随着 $$$k$$$ 的增加，$$$c_k$$$ 的值会发生怎样的变化？在这个问题中，你的任务是计算 $$$\max_{k \in \mathbb{N}} c_k$$$。
input: 第一行包含两个正整数 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$m$$$$$$(1 \leq n \leq 100\,000, 1 \leq m \leq 250\,000)$$$，分别表示节点数和边数。节点的编号从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$。请注意，这些不是节点的标签。
第二行包含$$$n$$$个整数，由前$$$n$$$个正整数排列而成，其中第$$$i$$$个数字代表节点$$$i$$$的初始标签。
接下来的 $$$m$$$ 行中的每一行都包含两个整数。这些行中的 $$$i$$$ 第三行包含两个不同的整数 $$$u_i$$$ 和 $$$v_i$$$$$$(1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n)$$$，即 $$$\{u_i, v_i\} \in E$$$。
输入将以这样一种方式设置，即不存在自循环、平行边或度为零的节点。
output: 打印所有正整数$$$k$$$的最大值$$$c_k$$$。

problems.hint: Consider the process of finding the MST. How many edges could appear before finding the $k$ -th edge?

legend: You are in the spaceship The Skeld with your fellow crewmates. However, while checking the central power system, you found out that one crucial wiring installation of the central power system has been sabotaged. To prevent an engine failure, you should quickly fix the installation.

The installation consists of $$$N$$$ nodes and $$$M=\frac{N(N-1)}{2}$$$ wires. All possible pairs of distinct nodes in the installation are connected with a wire. Originally, each of the $$$M$$$ wires had exactly one tag attached to it. Each tag has a positive integer value, and different tags may have the same value. However, due to the sabotage, all the tags were removed from the wires and left on the floor. Fortunately, you gathered all $$$M$$$ tags from the ground. Now, in order to fix the installation, you have to trigger the reboot sequence by re-attaching all the tags back to the wires twice.

For an installation where all wires have a tag on them, let's define the cost of an installation as the cost of its minimum spanning tree, that is, the minimum cost of a subset of wires such that all nodes are connected using only the given subset of wires. Here, the cost of the set of wires is defined as the sum of the tag values of all wires in the set.
The reboot sequence is triggered in two steps:
First, you should attach the tags to minimize the cost of the installation.
Then, after detaching all tags, you should attach the tags to maximize the cost of the installation.
Please compute the cost of each installation.
input: The first line of the input contains an integer $$$N$$$, representing the number of nodes. ($$$2 \le N \le 100$$$)
The second line of the input contains $$$M=\frac{N(N-1)}{2}$$$ positive integers $$$C_1, C_2, \cdots C_M$$$, representing the integer values of $$$M$$$ tags. ($$$1 \le C_i \le 2 \cdot 10^9$$$)
output: Output a single line containing two integers. The first should be the minimum possible cost of the installation, the second should be the maximum possible cost of the installation.

legend: 你和其他船员一起在斯凯德号飞船上。然而，在检查中央动力系统时，你们发现中央动力系统的一个关键线路装置被破坏了。为了防止发动机发生故障，您必须尽快修复该装置。

安装由 $$$N$$$ 节点和 $$$M=\frac{N(N-1)}{2}$$$ 导线组成。安装中所有可能的不同节点对都通过一根导线连接。最初，每根 $$$M$$$ 导线上只有一个标签。每个标签都有一个正整数值，不同的标签可能具有相同的值。然而，由于破坏，所有标签都从导线上移除了，留在了地上。幸运的是，你从地上收集了所有 $$$M$$$ 标签。现在，为了修复安装，你必须通过将所有标签重新连接到导线两次来触发重启序列。
对于所有导线都有标签的装置，我们将装置的成本定义为最小生成树的成本，即导线子集的最小成本，这样所有节点只需使用给定的导线子集即可连接。这里，导线集合的成本定义为集合中所有导线的标签值之和。
触发重启顺序分为两个步骤：
首先，应贴上标签，尽量减少安装成本。
然后，在卸下所有标签后，您应该附加标签，以最大限度地提高安装成本。
请计算每次安装的费用。
input: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$N$$$，表示节点的数量。($$$2 \le N \le 100$$$)
输入的第二行包含$$$M=\frac{N(N-1)}{2}$$$个正整数$$$C_1, C_2, \cdots C_M$$$，表示$$$M$$$标签的整数值。($$$1 \le C_i \le 2 \cdot 10^9$$$)
output: 输出包含两个整数的一行。第一个整数应为最小可能安装成本，第二个整数应为最大可能安装成本。

problems.hint: A lot of shortest paths.

legend: Alice and Bob are in the middle of a damn pandemic. They wanted to travel together somewhere for summer. However, they are in different countries and since the pandemic started, multiple flights have been canceled. What is worst, their respective countries do not allow tourists to enter, so they have to find another country to see each other. Nevertheless, they are allowed to use any country (including their residence countries) for stopovers.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/22aae2a330837f96a373ef48381033f037bd8785.png)

Alice and Bob have spent nearly all of their money on face masks, toilet paper, and disinfectant. Therefore, they need to minimize the total amount of money spent on flights, including the returning trip to their respective homes. Ironically, Alice and Bob are official members of the United Nihilistic Airlines League (UNAL), which has granted a special $$$k$$$-ticket to each of them. A $$$k$$$-ticket allows a passenger to take up to $$$k$$$ free flights, those tickets are personal and non-transferable.
Can you help them to find the country where they can see each other with minimal cost?
input: The first line consists of 2 integers separated by a space, $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$3$$$ $$$\leq$$$ $$$n,m$$$ $$$\leq$$$ $$$10^4$$$) — The number of countries, and the number of available flights, respectively.

The next line consists of 3 integers separated by a space, $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$0$$$ $$$\leq$$$ $$$a,b$$$ $$$ \lt $$$ $$$n$$$, $$$a \neq b$$$, $$$0$$$ $$$\leq$$$ $$$k$$$ $$$\le$$$ $$$10$$$) — The country where Alice lives, the country where Bob lives, and the amount of free flights available on each $$$k$$$-ticket, respectively.

The next $$$m$$$ lines contains 3 integers each: $$$u$$$, $$$v$$$ ($$$0$$$ $$$\leq$$$ $$$u,v$$$ $$$ \lt $$$ $$$n$$$, $$$u \neq v$$$) and $$$w$$$ ($$$1$$$ $$$\leq$$$ $$$w$$$ $$$\leq$$$ $$$10^3$$$) separated by a space, which represent a flight coming from $$$u$$$ into $$$v$$$ with cost $$$w$$$.
output: Print two integers separated by a space, the index of the country where Alice and Bob should travel and the total round trip cost for both Alice and Bob. if there are many possible countries with minimal cost print the one with the lowest index.
If Alice and Bob cannot see each other print ">:(".

legend: 爱丽丝和鲍勃正处于一场该死的大流行病中。他们本想暑假一起去某个地方旅行。然而，他们身处不同的国家，自从大流行病开始后，多趟航班都被取消了。最糟糕的是，他们各自的国家都不允许游客入境，所以他们只能另找一个国家见面。不过，他们可以在任何国家（包括他们的居住国）中途停留。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/22aae2a330837f96a373ef48381033f037bd8785.png)
Alice 和 Bob 几乎把所有的钱都花在了口罩、卫生纸和消毒剂上。因此，他们需要尽量减少机票的总花费，包括回家的路费。具有讽刺意味的是，Alice 和 Bob 是联合虚无航空联盟 (UNAL) 的正式成员，该联盟为他们每人颁发了一张特殊的 $$$k$$$ 机票。$$$k$$$ 机票允许乘客免费乘坐 $$$k$$$ 航班，这些机票是个人的，不可转让。
你能帮他们找到一个能让他们以最小的成本见面的国家吗？
input: 第一行由两个整数组成，中间用空格隔开，分别是 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$m$$$ ($$$3$$$ $$$\leq$$$ $$$n,m$$$ $$$\leq$$$ $$$10^4$$$）--国家数和可用航班数。
output: 打印两个用空格隔开的整数，即 Alice 和 Bob 应该去的国家的索引，以及 Alice 和 Bob 的往返总费用。
如果爱丽丝和鲍勃看不到彼此，请打印 “>:”(.

problems.hint: Not a lot transitions.

legend: Standard stack sizes in Minecraft are $$$2^6=64$$$ for most blocks and items, $$$2^4=16$$$ for select items, and $$$2^0=1$$$ for tools and special items. However, Mojang's latest update has a lot of bugs, forcing items to stack to exactly any integer power of $$$2$$$, including powers greater than $$$64$$$: $$$128$$$, $$$256$$$, and so on! Since you were down in your mineshaft before the update dropped, you decide to use the opportunity to start moving your supply of gems back to your base above ground.

You have diamonds and emeralds in the mineshaft's storage that you want to bring, but you can't put them in your inventory since you're carrying lots of other important items (i.e. Pigstep and deadbushes). But, you do have a bundle, a portable container that fits exactly $$$N$$$ items. Due to another bug in the update, you can only insert stacks of items in alternating order, but you can start with either diamonds or emeralds. For example, if you first insert a power-of-two stack of diamonds, the next stack you insert must be a power-of-two stack of emeralds.

For example, the bundle might be able to fit $$$4$$$ gems. There are $$$12$$$ possible ways to put them in, shown below. Note that each sequence of the same item must have a length matching some power of $$$2$$$; as such, a length of $$$3$$$ is unable to be added to the bundle.
DEDE, EDED, DDED, EEDE, DEED, EDDE, DEDD, EDEE, DDEE, EEDD, DDDD, EEEE

You're curious about how many different ways you could completely fill your bundle. Given the capacity of the bundle $$$N$$$, determine how many different ways the bundle can be filled. Assume that you have at least $$$N$$$ gems of each type.
input: The only line of input is integer $$$N$$$ $$$(1 \le N \le 10^5)$$$: the capacity of your bundle.
output: Output a single integer: the number of ways that you could fill your bundle $$$\text{mod}$$$ $$$10^9+7$$$.

legend: 我的世界中大多数方块和物品的标准堆叠大小为$$$2^6=64$$$，选择物品的标准堆叠大小为$$$2^4=16$$$，工具和特殊物品的标准堆叠大小为$$$2^0=1$$$。然而，Mojang的最新更新有很多错误，强制物品堆叠到$$$2$$$的任何整数幂，包括大于$$$64$$$的幂：$$$128$$$，$$$256$$$等等！由于你在更新之前在你的矿井里，你决定利用这个机会开始将你的宝石供应移回地面上的基地。
例如，bundle 可能能够容纳 $$$4$$$ 宝石。有 $$$12$$$ 种可能的方式来放置它们，如下所示。请注意，同一项目的每个序列的长度必须与 $$$2$$$ 的某个幂相匹配;因此，$$$3$$$ 的长度不能添加到 bundle 中。
DEDE, EDED, DDED, EEDE, DEED, EDDE, DEDD, EDEE, DDEE, EEDD, DDDD, EEEE
你很好奇有多少种不同的方法可以完全填满你的包。给定捆绑包的容量$$$N$$$，确定捆绑包可以通过多少种不同的方式填充。假设您至少拥有每种类型的$$$N$$$个宝石。
input: 唯一的输入行是整数 $$$N$$$$$$(1 \le N \le 10^5)$$$:你的 bundle 的容量。
output: 输出单个整数：您可以填充bundle $$$\text{mod}$$$ $$$10^9+7$$$的方法数。

problems.hint: The shortest path. What is the edge weight?

legend: During his vacation in Aracaju, Samuell decided to spend the morning swimming at Atalaia Beach, one of the city's postcards, famous for its beautiful and long stretch of sand.

When it was time to leave, a problem came up: with the sun high in the sky, he must cross the entire beach, from the sea to the boardwalk, and request an Uber. To avoid getting sunburned, Samuell plans to use the shadows of the beach umbrellas spread across the sand and choose a route that minimizes the distance walked under the sun.

Formally, the beach can be represented by the strip between two parallel lines: one is the line where the sea meets the sand ($$$y = 0$$$), and the other is the boardwalk ($$$y = H$$$), at distance $$$H$$$ from the first one. There are $$$N$$$ beach umbrellas; the $$$i$$$-th one casts a circular shadow with center $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$ and radius $$$r_i$$$.
Assume Samuell can swim freely underwater without being exposed to the sun, and can leave the water at any point on the sea line. Once on the sand, he can:
walk under the shadow of a beach umbrella, including moving directly to another one when their shadows touch or overlap;
leave the sand at any point on the boardwalk.
Help Samuell determine the minimum distance he must walk under the sun to reach the boardwalk.
input: The first line contains two integers $$$N$$$ and $$$H$$$ ($$$0 \leq N \leq 1000$$$, $$$1 \leq H \leq 10^{5}$$$), respectively the number of beach umbrellas and the distance between the sea line and the boardwalk.

Each of the next $$$N$$$ lines contains three integers $$$x_i$$$, $$$y_i$$$, and $$$r_i$$$ ($$$0 \leq x_i \leq 10^5$$$, $$$0 \leq y_i \leq H$$$, $$$1 \leq r_i \leq 10^{5}$$$), the center and radius of the $$$i$$$-th beach umbrella. A beach umbrella's shadow may extend beyond the sea line or the boardwalk.
output: Print a single real number: the minimum distance under the sun that Samuell must walk to cross the sand, from the sea to the boardwalk.
Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error with respect to the expected answer is at most $$$10^{-6}$$$.
note: Explanation for example 1
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/972c302b3b38763e22e730a007c1d277ede8e189.png)
In the first example, Samuell can take a route where he walks $$$3\sqrt{5} - 4$$$ under the sun.
Explanation for example 2
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/746ae0cf78382eb085d87ae22650d7434f096e73.png)

In the second example, Samuell walks one unit under the sun to reach the first shadow. The two shadows touch, allowing him to move from one to the other without being exposed. Then he walks one more unit to the boardwalk. Therefore, the total distance under the sun is $$$1 + 1 = 2$$$.
Explanation for example 3
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3cc299a3fce32b4cbef76be28478e69a649bd11c.png)

In the third example, the only shadow has radius $$$5$$$ and center $$$(3, 3)$$$. Since it reaches both the sea line and the boardwalk, Samuell can cross the whole beach while staying in the shadow. Therefore, the distance walked under the sun is $$$0$$$.

legend: 当离开的时候，一个问题出现了：太阳高高挂在天空中，他必须穿过整个海滩，从大海到木板路，并要求一辆优步。为了避免被晒伤，塞缪尔计划利用沙滩伞的阴影散布在沙滩上，并选择一条最短的路线，在阳光下行走的距离。
形式上，海滩可以用两条平行线之间的条带来表示：一条是海水与沙子相遇的线($$$y = 0$$$），另一条是木板路($$$y = H$$$），与第一条线的距离为$$$H$$$。有$$$N$$$个沙滩伞，第$$$i$$$个沙滩伞投射出圆心为$$$(x_i, y_i)$$$、半径为$$$r_i$$$的圆形阴影。
在海滩遮阳伞的阴影下行走，包括当他们的影子相触或重叠时直接移动到另一把遮阳伞下;
在木板路上的任何位置离开沙子。
帮助塞缪尔确定他在阳光下必须走到木板路的最小距离。
input: 第一行包含两个整数 $$$N$$$ 和 $$$H$$$($$$0 \leq N \leq 1000$$$,$$$1 \leq H \leq 10^{5}$$$)，分别是海滩遮阳伞的数量和海岸线与木板步道之间的距离。
接下来的每一行$$$N$$$包含三个整数$$$x_i$$$， $$$y_i$$$和$$$r_i$$$ ($$$0 \leq x_i \leq 10^5$$$, $$$0 \leq y_i \leq H$$$, $$$1 \leq r_i \leq 10^{5}$$$)，即第$$$i$$$伞的中心和半径。沙滩伞的阴影可能会延伸到海岸线或木板路之外。
output: 打印一个实数：太阳下塞缪尔穿过沙滩必须走的最小距离，从大海到木板路。
如果你的答案与预期答案的绝对或相对误差至多为 $$$10^{-6}$$$，则将被认为是正确的。
note: 示例1的解释
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/972c302b3b38763e22e730a007c1d277ede8e189.png)
在第一个例子中，Samuell可以选择他在阳光下行走的路线$$$3\sqrt{5} - 4$$$。
示例2的解释
在第二个例子中，Samuel 在阳光下走了一个单位到达第一个阴影。两个阴影相接，使他能够从一个阴影移动到另一个阴影而不被发现。然后他又走了一个单位到达木板路。因此，阳光下的总距离为 $$$1 + 1 = 2$$$。
示例 3 的解释
在第三个例子中，唯一的阴影半径为 $$$5$$$，中心为 $$$(3, 3)$$$。由于它同时到达海岸线和木板路，塞缪尔可以在阴影中穿越整个海滩。因此，在阳光下行走的距离为 $$$0$$$。

statement.title: E. Krosh and expected value problem

legend: Krosh has been learning probability theory and came up with the following problem: consider an array of $$$n$$$ natural numbers from $$$1$$$ to $$$x$$$ and natural number $$$k$$$. Then $$$k$$$ steps follow, on each step we take current array and simultaneously insert a random number from $$$1$$$ to $$$x$$$ between every pair of adjacent numbers, these numbers are chosen equiprobably and independently on each step and in each step. Krosh is interested what is expected number of segments consisting of the equal numbers after $$$k$$$ steps of the algorithm? For example, if $$$a = [1, 2, 4, 1, 1, 5, 5, 6]$$$, $$$x = 6$$$, then number of segments is $$$6$$$. After one step we can obtain the array: $$$[1, 5, 2, 2, 4, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 5, 6, 5, 2, 6]$$$ with $$$11$$$ segments.
input: In first line you are given three natural numbers $$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le x \le 10^9$$$, $$$0 \le k \le 10^9$$$. In next line you are given an array of $$$n$$$ natural numbers from $$$1$$$ to $$$x$$$.
output: Output answer modulo $$$10^9+7$$$. Answer can be represented as $$$P/Q$$$, where $$$P$$$ and $$$Q$$$ are non-negative integers and $$$Q  \gt  0$$$. Output $$$P * Q^{-1}$$$ modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.

legend: Krosh 一直在学习概率论，并提出了以下问题：考虑一个由 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$x$$$ 的自然数 $$$n$$$ 和自然数 $$$k$$$ 组成的数组。然后是 $$$k$$$ 步骤，在每个步骤中，我们取当前数组，并同时在每对相邻的数之间插入一个 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$x$$$ 的随机数，这些数在每个步骤和每个步骤中都是等概率和独立选择的。Krosh 感兴趣的是，在算法的 $$$k$$$ 步骤之后，由相等数组成的段的预期数量是多少？例如，如果 $$$a = [1, 2, 4, 1, 1, 5, 5, 6]$$$,$$$x = 6$$$，那么段的数量是 $$$6$$$。经过一步，我们可以得到包含 $$$11$$$ 段的数组 $$$[1, 5, 2, 2, 4, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 5, 6, 5, 2, 6]$$$。
input: 在第一行中，我们给出了三个自然数 $$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$、$$$1 \le x \le 10^9$$$、$$$0 \le k \le 10^9$$$。在下一行中，我们给出了一个 $$$n$$$ 自然数的数组，范围从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$x$$$。

problems.hint: $k$ -th time you use a ski, how many steps could you make?

legend: Esomer loves skiing. However, he hates ski lifts because they are very long and always very cold. Determined not to suffer any longer, he has tried to come up with a route that minimizes the time spent on ski lifts. Unfortunately, he is not very good at interpreting the map of the pistes, so he has asked for your help.

The ski resort that Esomer visits can be represented as a directed acyclic graph with $$$n$$$ nodes and $$$m$$$ edges (the pistes). Additionally, there are $$$k$$$ ski lifts that connect node $$$a$$$ to node $$$b$$$. Interestingly, all ski lifts satisfy the condition that it is always possible to reach $$$a$$$ from $$$b$$$ without using any ski lift. It takes Esomer $$$1$$$ minute to traverse a piste or use a ski lift.

Esomer is interested in how much time he needs to spend on ski lifts in order to spend a total of $$$x$$$ minutes at the ski resort, without stopping at any node even for a second, while starting at node $$$y$$$. Esomer can finish his route at any node and leave for home as soon as he has spent the required $$$x$$$ minutes.
Please help Esomer.
input: The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$, the number of test cases. ($$$1 \le t \le 100$$$).
For each test case, the first line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$ and $$$k$$$. ($$$2 \le n \le 10^5$$$; $$$1 \le m \le \min(10^5, \frac{n \cdot (n-1)}{2})$$$; $$$1 \le k \le 10^2$$$).
Then, there are $$$m$$$ lines, each containing two integers, $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$, indicating that there is an edge from $$$u$$$ to $$$v$$$. ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$).
It is guaranteed that the graph formed by the $$$m$$$ edges is acyclic.
Next, there are $$$k$$$ lines, each containing two integers, $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, indicating that there is a ski lift from $$$a$$$ to $$$b$$$. ($$$1 \le a, b \le n$$$; $$$a \neq b$$$).
It is guaranteed that it is possible to reach $$$a$$$ from $$$b$$$ without using any ski lift.

Finally, there is a line containing two integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$, the number of minutes Esomer wants to spend at the ski resort, and the node at which he starts, respectively. ($$$1 \le x \le 10^9$$$; $$$1 \le y \le n$$$). It is guaranteed that Esomer can reach a ski lift from node $$$y$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ over all test cases is at most $$$10^5$$$, while the sum of $$$k$$$ over all test cases is at most $$$10^2$$$.
output: For each test case, you should print an integer $$$s$$$, the minimum number of minutes Esomer needs to spend on ski lifts in order to spend a total of $$$x$$$ minutes at the ski resort.
note: Problem idea: Esomer

legend: 埃索梅尔喜欢滑雪。然而，他讨厌滑雪缆车，因为它们非常长，而且总是非常冷。为了不再受苦，他试图找到一条能最大限度减少滑雪缆车时间的路线。不幸的是，他不太擅长解读滑雪道地图，所以他向你寻求帮助。
Esomer访问的滑雪场可以表示为具有$$$n$$$个节点和$$$m$$$条边(滑雪道）的有向无环图。此外，还有连接节点$$$a$$$和节点$$$b$$$的$$$k$$$滑雪缆车。有趣的是，所有的滑雪缆车都满足一个条件，即在不使用任何滑雪缆车的情况下，总是可以从$$$b$$$到达$$$a$$$。穿越雪道或使用滑雪缆车需要Esomer $$$1$$$分钟。
Esomer 想知道，从节点 $$$y$$$ 开始，他需要在滑雪缆车上花费多少时间，才能在滑雪胜地总共花费 $$$x$$$ 分钟，而不在任何节点停留哪怕一秒钟。埃斯莫可以在任何一个节点完成他的路线，一旦他花费了所需的 $$$x$$$ 分钟，他就可以离开回家。
请帮帮埃索莫。
input: 第一行包含一个整数$$$t$$$，测试用例的数量。($$$1 \le t \le 100$$$)。
然后，存在 $$$m$$$ 行，每行包含两个整数 $$$u$$$ 和 $$$v$$$，表明存在从 $$$u$$$ 到 $$$v$$$ 的边界。($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$)。
保证由$$$m$$$条边构成的图是无环的。
接下来是$$$k$$$行，每一行包含两个整数$$$a$$$和$$$b$$$，表示从$$$a$$$到$$$b$$$有一个滑雪缆车。($$$1 \le a, b \le n$$$; $$$a \neq b$$$)。
保证可以从 $$$b$$$ 到达 $$$a$$$，而无需使用任何滑雪缆车。
最后，有一行包含两个整数$$$x$$$和$$$y$$$，分别是Esomer想要在滑雪场花费的分钟数和他开始的节点。($$$1 \le x \le 10^9$$$; $$$1 \le y \le n$$$)。保证Esomer可以从节点$$$y$$$到达滑雪缆车。
保证所有测试用例的 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$m$$$ 之和至多为 $$$10^5$$$，而所有测试用例的 $$$k$$$ 之和至多为 $$$10^2$$$。
output: 对于每个测试用例，你应该打印一个整数 $$$s$$$，即 Esomer 需要在滑雪缆车上花费的最小分钟数，以便在滑雪场总共花费 $$$x$$$ 分钟。

problems.hint: What does the four corners belong to?

legend: Bethany would like to tile her bathroom. The bathroom has width $$$w$$$ centimeters and length $$$l$$$ centimeters. If Bethany simply used the basic tiles of size $$$1 \times 1$$$ centimeters, she would use $$$w \cdot l$$$ of them.
However, she has something different in mind.
On the interior of the floor she wants to use the $$$1 \times 1$$$ tiles. She needs exactly $$$(w-2) \cdot (l-2)$$$ of these.
On the floor boundary she wants to use tiles of size $$$1 \times a$$$ for some positive integer $$$a$$$. The tiles can also be rotated by $$$90$$$ degrees.
For which values of $$$a$$$ can Bethany tile the bathroom floor as described? Note that $$$a$$$ can also be $$$1$$$.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 100$$$) — the number of test cases. The descriptions of the $$$t$$$ test cases follow.
Each test case consist of a single line, which contains two integers $$$w$$$, $$$l$$$ ($$$3 \leq w, l \leq 10^{9}$$$) — the dimensions of the bathroom.
output: For each test case, print an integer $$$k$$$ ($$$0\le k$$$) — the number of valid values of $$$a$$$ for the given test case — followed by $$$k$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2,\dots, a_k$$$ ($$$1\le a_i$$$) — the valid values of $$$a$$$. The values $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$$$ have to be sorted from smallest to largest.
It is guaranteed that under the problem constraints, the output contains at most $$$200\,000$$$ integers.
note: In the first test case, the bathroom is $$$3$$$ centimeters wide and $$$5$$$ centimeters long. There are three values of $$$a$$$ such that Bethany can tile the floor as described in the statement, namely $$$a=1$$$, $$$a=2$$$ and $$$a=3$$$. The three tilings are represented in the following pictures.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/752df8f3030b032712b9ac93b08960db84e3b98a.png)

legend: 贝萨妮想给浴室铺瓷砖。浴室的宽度是 $$$w$$$ 厘米，长度是 $$$l$$$ 厘米。如果贝萨妮只用 $$$1 \times 1$$$ 厘米大小的基本瓷砖，她会用 $$$w \cdot l$$$。
然而，她有不同的想法。
在地板边界上，她希望使用尺寸为 $$$1 \times a$$$ 的瓷砖，其大小为某个正整数 $$$a$$$。瓷砖还可以旋转 $$$90$$$ 度。
对于 $$$a$$$ 的哪些值，贝瑟尼可以按照描述的方式铺设浴室地板？注意 $$$a$$$ 也可以是 $$$1$$$。
input: 每个测试包含多个测试用例。第一行包含一个整数$$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 100$$$）—测试用例的数量。下面是对$$$t$$$测试用例的描述。
每个测试用例由单行组成，其中包含两个整数$$$w$$$， $$$l$$$ ($$$3 \leq w, l \leq 10^{9}$$$) -浴室的尺寸。
output: 对于每个测试用例，打印一个整数 $$$k$$$($$$0\le k$$$)——给定测试用例中 $$$a$$$ 的有效值数——后面跟着 $$$k$$$ 整数 $$$a_1, a_2,\dots, a_k$$$($$$1\le a_i$$$)——$$$a$$$ 的有效值。$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$$$ 值必须从最小到最大进行排序。
保证在问题约束条件下，输出最多包含 $$$200\,000$$$ 个整数。
note: 在第一个测试案例中，浴室宽$$$3$$$厘米，长$$$5$$$厘米。$$$a$$$有三个值，即$$$a=1$$$、$$$a=2$$$和$$$a=3$$$，使得Bethany可以如声明中所述铺设地板。三个平铺在下面的图片中表示。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/752df8f3030b032712b9ac93b08960db84e3b98a.png)

problems.hint: Find some characteristics.

legend: There are $$$n$$$ equidistant antennas on a line, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. Each antenna has a power rating, the power of the $$$i$$$-th antenna is $$$p_i$$$.

The $$$i$$$-th and the $$$j$$$-th antenna can communicate directly if and only if their distance is at most the minimum of their powers, i.e., $$$|i-j| \leq \min(p_i, p_j)$$$. Sending a message directly between two such antennas takes $$$1$$$ second.
What is the minimum amount of time necessary to send a message from antenna $$$a$$$ to antenna $$$b$$$, possibly using other antennas as relays?
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 100\,000$$$) — the number of test cases. The descriptions of the $$$t$$$ test cases follow.
The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$ ($$$1 \leq a, b \leq n \leq 200\,000$$$) — the number of antennas, and the origin and target antenna.
The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq p_i \leq n$$$) — the powers of the antennas.
The sum of the values of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$200\,000$$$.
output: For each test case, print the number of seconds needed to trasmit a message from $$$a$$$ to $$$b$$$. It can be shown that under the problem constraints, it is always possible to send such a message.
note: In the first test case, we must send a message from antenna $$$2$$$ to antenna $$$9$$$. A sequence of communications requiring $$$4$$$ seconds, which is the minimum possible amount of time, is the following:
In $$$1$$$ second we send the message from antenna $$$2$$$ to antenna $$$1$$$. This is possible since $$$|2-1|\le \min(1, 4) = \min(p_2, p_1)$$$.
In $$$1$$$ second we send the message from antenna $$$1$$$ to antenna $$$5$$$. This is possible since $$$|1-5|\le \min(4, 5) = \min(p_1, p_5)$$$.
In $$$1$$$ second we send the message from antenna $$$5$$$ to antenna $$$10$$$. This is possible since $$$|5-10|\le \min(5, 5) = \min(p_5, p_{10})$$$.
In $$$1$$$ second we send the message from antenna $$$10$$$ to antenna $$$9$$$. This is possible since $$$|10-9|\le \min(5, 1) = \min(p_{10}, p_9)$$$.

legend: 一条线上有 $$$n$$$ 个等距天线，编号从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$。每个天线都有一个额定功率，$$$i$$$-th 天线的功率为 $$$p_i$$$。
$$$i$$$ 和 $$$j$$$ 天线可以直接通信，当且仅当它们之间的距离最大值为其功率的最小值，即 $$$|i-j| \leq \min(p_i, p_j)$$$。直接在两个这样的天线之间发送消息需要 $$$1$$$ 秒。
从天线$$$a$$$向天线$$$b$$$发送消息(可能使用其他天线作为中继）所需的最短时间是多少？
input: 每个测试包含多个测试用例。第一行包含一个整数$$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 100\,000$$$）—测试用例的数量。下面是对$$$t$$$测试用例的描述。
每个测试用例的第一行包含三个整数$$$n$$$、$$$a$$$、$$$b$$$($$$1 \leq a, b \leq n \leq 200\,000$$$）——天线的数量，以及原点和目标天线。
第二行包含 $$$n$$$ 整数 $$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq p_i \leq n$$$）--天线的幂。
所有测试用例中 $$$n$$$ 值的总和不超过 $$$200\,000$$$。
output: 对于每个测试用例，打印将消息从$$$a$$$传输到$$$b$$$所需的秒数。可以看出，在问题约束条件下，总是可以发送这样的消息。
note: 在第一个测试案例中，我们必须从天线$$$2$$$向天线$$$9$$$发送消息。需要$$$4$$$秒(最小可能时间量）的通信序列如下:
在 $$$1$$$ 中，我们第二次将信息从天线 $$$2$$$ 发送到天线 $$$1$$$。这在 $$$|2-1|\le \min(1, 4) = \min(p_2, p_1)$$$ 中是可能的。

legend: A wild basilisk just appeared at your doorstep. You are not entirely sure what a basilisk is and you wonder whether it evolved from your favorite animal, the weasel.

How can you find out whether basilisks evolved from weasels? Certainly, a good first step is to sequence both of their DNAs. Then you can try to check whether there is a sequence of possible mutations from the DNA of the weasel to the DNA of the basilisk.

Your friend Ron is a talented alchemist and has studied DNA sequences in many of his experiments. He has found out that DNA strings consist of the letters A, B and C and that single mutations can only remove or add substrings at any position in the string (a substring is a contiguous sequence of characters). The substrings that can be removed or added by a mutation are AA, BB, CC, ABAB or BCBC. During a sequence of mutations a DNA string may even become empty.

Ron has agreed to sequence the DNA of the weasel and the basilisk for you, but finding out whether there is a sequence of possible mutations that leads from one to the other is too difficult for him, so you have to do it on your own.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 100$$$) — the number of test cases. The descriptions of the $$$t$$$ test cases follow.
The first line of each test case contains a string $$$u$$$ ($$$1\le |u|\le 200$$$) — the DNA of the weasel.
The second line of each test case contains a string $$$v$$$ ($$$1\le |v|\le 200$$$) — the DNA of the basilisk.
The values $$$|u|$$$, $$$|v|$$$ denote the lengths of the strings $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that both strings $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ consist of the letters A, B and C.
output: For each test case, print YES if there is a sequence of mutations to get from $$$u$$$ to $$$v$$$ and NO otherwise.

legend: 一只野生蛇怪刚刚出现在你家门口。你不完全确定蛇怪是什么，你想知道它是不是从你最喜欢的动物黄鼠狼进化而来的。
如何才能知道玄武鱼是否由黄鼠狼进化而来？当然，第一步是对它们的 DNA 进行测序。然后，你可以尝试检查从黄鼠狼的 DNA 到玄武鱼的 DNA 是否存在一个可能的变异序列。
你的朋友罗恩是一位才华横溢的炼金术士，他在许多实验中研究了 DNA 序列。他发现 DNA 序列由字母 A、B 和 C 组成，而单个突变只能在序列的任何位置删除或添加子串 (子串是一个连续的字符序列)。突变可以删除或添加的子串包括 AA、BB、CC、ABAB 或 BCBC。在一系列突变过程中，DNA 序列甚至可能变成空的。
罗恩已经同意为你对黄鼠狼和蛇怪的DNA进行测序，但找出是否存在一系列可能的突变，导致从一个到另一个对他来说太难了，所以你必须自己做。
input: 每个测试包含多个测试用例。第一行包含一个整数 $$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 100$$$）--测试用例的数量。下面是 $$$t$$$ 测试用例的说明。
每个测试用例的第一行包含一个字符串$$$u$$$($$$1\le |u|\le 200$$$）—黄鼠狼的DNA。
每个测试用例的第二行都包含一个字符串 $$$v$$$ ($$$1\le |v|\le 200$$$）--玄武岩的 DNA。
值 $$$|u|$$$、$$$|v|$$$ 表示字符串 $$$u$$$ 和 $$$v$$$ 的长度。保证字符串 $$$u$$$ 和 $$$v$$$ 都由字母 A、B 和 C 组成。
output: 对于每个测试用例，如果存在从$$$u$$$到$$$v$$$的突变序列，则打印“是”，否则打印“否”。

problems.hint: Find some characteristics.

legend: Today the $$$n^2$$$ contestants of EUC have gathered outside the venue to take a drone photo. Jennifer, the social media manager for the event, has arranged them into an $$$n\times n$$$ square. Being very good at her job, she knows that the contestant standing on the intersection of the $$$i$$$-th row with the $$$j$$$-th column is $$$a_{i,j}$$$ years old. Coincidentally, she notices that no two contestants have the same age, and that everyone is between $$$1$$$ and $$$n^2$$$ years old.

Jennifer is planning to have some contestants hold a banner with the ICPC logo parallel to the ground, so that it is clearly visible in the aerial picture. Here are the steps that she is going to follow in order to take the perfect EUC drone photo.
First of all, Jennifer is going to select four contestants standing on the vertices of an axis-aligned rectangle.
Then, she will have the two younger contestants hold one of the poles, while the two older contestants will hold the other pole.
Finally, she will unfold the banner, using the poles to support its two ends. Obviously, this can only be done if the two poles are parallel and do not cross, as shown in the pictures below.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/57b5894ab01c60bf268f7ca009abe6aac86b8333.png)

Being very indecisive, Jennifer would like to try out all possible arrangements for the banner, but she is worried that this may cause the contestants to be late for the competition. How many different ways are there to choose the four contestants holding the poles in order to take a perfect photo? Two choices are considered different if at least one contestant is included in one but not the other.
input: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2\le n \le 1500$$$).
The next $$$n$$$ lines describe the ages of the contestants. Specifically, the $$$i$$$-th line contains the integers $$$a_{i,1},a_{i,2},\ldots,a_{i,n}$$$ ($$$1\le a_{i,j}\le n^2$$$).

It is guaranteed that $$$a_{i,j}
eq a_{k,l}$$$ if $$$i
eq k$$$ or $$$j
eq l$$$.
output: Print the number of ways for Jennifer to choose the four contestants holding the poles.
note: In the first sample, there are $$$4$$$ contestants, arranged as follows.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d546103046d574eed55457072322fc4d14fa48b1.png)

There is only one way to choose four contestants, with one pole held by contestants aged $$$1$$$ and $$$2$$$ and the other one by contestants aged $$$3$$$ and $$$4$$$. But then, as we can see in the picture, the poles cross.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1b17e53062c04413ac2e22103e27126499116393.png)
Since there is no valid way to choose four contestants, the answer is $$$0$$$.
In the second sample, the $$$4$$$ contestants are arranged as follows.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/56a93c7230eb432a43828c0380a6316f3d0519f1.png)
Once again, there is only one way to choose four contestants, but this time the poles don't cross.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/52d1026b34935125e3f33df7a40e55fedd8965f7.png)
Therefore, the answer is $$$1$$$.
In the third sample, the $$$9$$$ contestants are arranged as follows.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fbf791ae257ca64e0fe5f29e05cb16251e52196b.png)
There are $$$6$$$ ways of choosing four contestants so that the poles don't cross, as shown in the following pictures.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/44b6e0d2f1cd8712da75d7b60c1c3ce84f778741.png)

legend: 今天，EUC 的 $$$n^2$$$ 参赛者聚集在会场外拍摄无人机照片。活动的社交媒体经理珍妮弗把他们排成了一个 $$$n\times n$$$ 正方形。由于她的工作非常出色，她知道站在第 $$$i$$$ 行和第 $$$j$$$ 列交叉点上的参赛者是 $$$a_{i,j}$$$ 岁。巧合的是，她注意到没有两个参赛者的年龄相同，每个人的年龄都在 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n^2$$$ 岁之间。
Jennifer 计划让一些参赛者举着印有 ICPC 标志的横幅，横幅与地面平行，以便在航拍照片中清晰可见。以下是她将采取的步骤，以拍摄完美的 EUC 无人机照片。
首先，詹妮弗要选出四名选手站在一个轴向矩形的顶点上。
然后，她会让两名年龄较小的选手握住其中一根杆子，而两名年龄较大的选手则握住另一根杆子。
最后，她将展开横幅，用杆子支撑其两端。显然，这只能在两极平行且不交叉的情况下实现，如下图所示。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/57b5894ab01c60bf268f7ca009abe6aac86b8333.png)
珍妮弗非常优柔寡断，她想尝试所有可能的横幅安排，但她担心这样会导致参赛者在比赛中迟到。为了拍出一张完美的照片，有多少种不同的方法来选择手持杆子的四位参赛者？如果至少有一名参赛者参加了其中一种选择，而另一种选择没有参加，那么这两种选择就被认为是不同的。
input: 第一行包含单个整数 $$$n$$$($$$2\le n \le 1500$$$)。
接下来的 $$$n$$$ 行描述了参赛者的年龄。具体来说，$$$i$$$ 第三行包含整数 $$$a_{i,1},a_{i,2},\ldots,a_{i,n}$$$($$$1\le a_{i,j}\le n^2$$$)。

保证$$$a_{i,j}
eq a_{k,l}$$$如果$$$i
eq k$$$或$$$j
eq l$$$。
output: 打印出詹妮弗选择四名手拿杆子的选手的方法数。
note: 在第一个样本中，有 $$$4$$$ 参赛者，排列如下。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d546103046d574eed55457072322fc4d14fa48b1.png)
四名选手只有一种选择方式，年龄为$$$1$$$、$$$2$$$的选手持一杆，年龄为$$$3$$$、$$$4$$$的选手持一杆。但是，正如我们在图中看到的，两极交叉。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1b17e53062c04413ac2e22103e27126499116393.png)
由于没有有效的方法选出四位参赛者，所以答案是$$$0$$$。
在第二个样本中，$$$4$$$ 参赛者的排列如下。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/56a93c7230eb432a43828c0380a6316f3d0519f1.png)
再一次，只有一种方法可以选出四位参赛者，但这次两极不会交叉。
在第三个样本中，$$$9$$$ 参赛者的排列如下。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fbf791ae257ca64e0fe5f29e05cb16251e52196b.png)
有 $$$6$$$ 种方法来选择四名参赛者，以确保两极不会相交，如下图所示。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/44b6e0d2f1cd8712da75d7b60c1c3ce84f778741.png)

problems.hint: The best position.

legend: Apples originated in the region of the Tian Shan Mountains of Kazakhstan. The name of the largest city in the country, Almaty, is often translated as "full of apples". After discovering this interesting fact, Harada and Teos, the biggest fans of apples in the world, decided to travel to Almaty. They now need your help preparing their luggage!

They will only take one bag, which can be seen as a 3D box from $$$(0, 0, 0)$$$ to $$$(x, y, z)$$$. Each of them will only put one object in the bag, an apple! Teos has already placed his apple inside the bag. Teos' apple can be seen as a 3D sphere with its center at $$$(tx, ty, tz)$$$ and radius $$$r$$$. Although the apple may be "floating" in the air, it is guaranteed to be entirely contained inside the bag. Now Harada wonders what is the largest apple, i.e., a 3D sphere, that can fit inside the box. Clearly, the two apples can touch each other but must not intersect at any point.
input: The first line contains three integers $$$1 \leq x, y, z \leq 10^9$$$, the dimensions of their luggage. The second line contains three floating-point numbers $$$0 \leq tx, ty, tz \leq 10^9$$$, the coordinates of the center of Teos' apple. The third line contains one floating-point number $$$10^{-9} \leq r \leq 10^9$$$, the radius of Teos' apple. It is guaranteed that Teos' apple is entirely contained within the luggage.
output: Output a single floating-point number: the radius of the largest 3D sphere that can be placed inside the luggage. The answer will be considered correct if the absolute or relative error is less than or equal to $$$10^{-6}$$$.
We recommend you print the answer with at least 15 decimal places. For this use:
printf(".15%lf\n", answer); in C;
cout << setprecision(15) << fixed << res << endl; in C++;
print("%.15f" % answer) in Python.
note: In the first test case, Harada can place an apple of radius $$$0.5$$$ at $$$(1.5, 0.5, 0.5)$$$. Any apple with radius greater than $$$0.5$$$ cannot be placed in the bag satisfying the statement constraints.

legend: 苹果原产于哈萨克斯坦的天山地区。这个国家最大的城市阿拉木图的名字通常被翻译为“满是苹果”。在发现这个有趣的事实后，原田和特奥斯，世界上最大的苹果粉丝，决定前往阿拉木图。他们现在需要你帮他们准备行李！

他们只拿一个袋子，这个袋子可以看作是从 $$$(0, 0, 0)$$$ 到 $$$(x, y, z)$$$ 的三维盒子。他们每人只在袋子里放一个东西，一个苹果！提奥斯已经把他的苹果放进了袋子里。提奥斯的苹果可以看作一个三维球体，它的中心在$$$(tx, ty, tz)$$$，半径为$$$r$$$。虽然苹果可能 "漂浮 "在空中，但可以保证它完全被装在袋子里。现在，原田想知道能装在盒子里的最大苹果(即三维球体）是多少。显然，两个苹果可以相互接触，但不能有任何交点。
input: 第一行包含三个整数 $$$1 \leq x, y, z \leq 10^9$$$，即他们行李箱的尺寸。第二行包含三个浮点数 $$$0 \leq tx, ty, tz \leq 10^9$$$，即 Teos 苹果的中心坐标。第三行包含一个浮点数 $$$10^{-9} \leq r \leq 10^9$$$，即 Teos 苹果的半径。确保 Teos 苹果完全包含在行李箱中。
output: 输出单个浮点数：可以放置在行李箱内的最大3D球体的半径。如果绝对或相对误差小于或等于$$$10^{-6}$$$，则认为答案正确。
我们建议您在打印答案时至少保留小数点后 15 位。为此请使用
printf(".15%lf\n", answer);在 C 语言中;
Cout << setprecision(15) << fixed << res << endl；在c++中;
用Python打印（“%.15f ”%答案）。
note: 在第一个测试案例中，原田可以在 $$$(1.5, 0.5, 0.5)$$$ 处放置一个半径为 $$$0.5$$$ 的苹果。任何半径大于 $$$0.5$$$ 的苹果都无法放入满足语句限制的袋子中。

problems.hint: Into simple numbers. And some numbers don't need to be considered.

statement.title: A. Eh Seedie, Hot Bel Kherej

legend: Humam (AKA Homam) goes fishing to put food on the table. One day, while using his fishing rod, he caught a bottle instead of a fish. Inside the bottle, he found a treasure map, and he was thrilled to discover the hidden treasure, leading him to stop fishing forever after.

He took his friend, Wael, saddled their horses, and went to the castle where the treasure was buried. They spent a week deciphering the riddles that led to the exact location of the treasure. Once they did, they started digging until they finally found the treasure, a buried array!

Both disappointed that the treasure was not money, gold or any valuable items, they started packing their things to head home. While doing so, Humam thought that he would take the array with him as a remembrance of this journey. Wael, not really caring about taking the array or leaving it, said: "Eh seedie, hot bel kherej". The kherej of Humam's horse was so small to fit the whole array, so he wanted to take a subset of its elements.
Humam thinks that a set of integer numbers is $$$\textit{good}$$$ if their product is divisible by $$$x$$$, where $$$x$$$ is Humam's lucky number.
Humam and Wael wanted to head home before it's dark. They want to find the minimum size of a subset of the buried array where it is $$$\textit{good}$$$. Can you help them?
a subset of an array $$$a$$$ is an array $$$b$$$ that can be obtained by removing zero or more elements from $$$a$$$.
input: The first line of the input contains two space-separated integer numbers $$$n$$$ and $$$x$$$ $$$(1 \le n \le 2\times 10^6, 1 \le x \le 10^9)$$$. The size of the buried array and Humam's lucky number, respectively.
The second line contains $$$n$$$ space-separated integer numbers $$$a_1, a_2 \dots a_n$$$ $$$(1 \le a_i \le 10^{18})$$$, where $$$a_i$$$ is the $$$i-th$$$ integer number in the buried array.
As the input file is large, consider using fast I/O
output: Print a single integer number. The minimum size of a subset of the buried array where it is $$$\textit{good}$$$, or $$$-1$$$ if there is no such subset.

legend: Humam（又名Homam）去钓鱼把食物放在桌子上。一天，他用钓竿钓到的不是鱼，而是一个瓶子。在瓶子里，他发现了一张藏宝图，他很兴奋地发现了隐藏的宝藏，这使他从此再也不钓鱼了。
他带着朋友瓦伊尔，给他们的马装上马鞍，前往埋藏宝藏的城堡。他们花了一周时间破解谜题，找到了宝藏的确切位置。一旦解开谜题，他们就开始挖掘，直到最终发现了宝藏——一个埋藏的阵列！
宝藏不是金钱、黄金或任何贵重物品，两人都很失望，于是开始收拾东西准备回家。在收拾行李的时候，胡马姆想把这个阵法带走，作为这次旅行的纪念。瓦埃勒并不在意要不要带走阵法，他说他说："Eh seedie, hot bel kherej"。胡马姆的马厩太小，装不下整个阵列，所以他想带走其中的一部分。
Humam 认为，如果一组整数的乘积可以被 $$$x$$$ 整除，那么这组整数就是 $$$\textit{good}$$$，其中 $$$x$$$ 是 Humam 的幸运数。
Humam和Wael想在天黑前回家。他们想要找到隐藏数组子集的最小大小，其中它是$$$\textit{good}$$$。你能帮助他们吗？
数组$$$a$$$的子集是从$$$a$$$中删除零个或多个元素后得到的数组$$$b$$$。
input: 输入的第一行包含两个空格分隔的整数 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$x$$$$$$(1 \le n \le 2\times 10^6, 1 \le x \le 10^9)$$$。分别是隐藏阵列的大小和 Humam 的幸运数。
第二行包含$$$n$$$空格分隔的整数$$$a_1, a_2 \dots a_n$$$$$$(1 \le a_i \le 10^{18})$$$，其中$$$a_i$$$是隐藏数组中的$$$i-th$$$整数。
由于输入文件较大，应考虑使用快速 I/O
output: 打印一个整数。隐藏数组的一个子集的最小大小，其中包含 $$$\textit{good}$$$，如果没有这样的子集，则为 $$$-1$$$。

problems.hint: Even $n$ -s and odd $n$ -s.

legend: If you ask Doludu and DoIudu what their favorite shape is, they will definitely say it is a hexagon. Because they really love hexagons so much, no matter what object it is, they always want to design it in a hexagonal shape, and game items are no exception.

Today, they are going to play a game. In this game, there are $$$N$$$ hexagonal blocks lined up in a row at the beginning, and these hexagonal blocks are divided into blue and red. After the game starts, the two of them will take turns to make a move, with Doludu going first. When it is a player's turn, he must remove either the leftmost or the rightmost block among the currently remaining blocks. At the moment when only one block is left, the game ends. If this block is blue, Doludu wins; otherwise, DoIudu wins.
Both Doludu and DoIudu are extremely smart and will definitely use the optimal strategy to play this game. Based on the initial colors of the $$$N$$$ blocks, please determine who will win among them.
input: The first line of the input contains an integer $$$T$$$, representing that Doludu and DoIudu will play $$$T$$$ games.

Next are the details of each game in order. The information for a single game consists of two lines. The first line contains an integer $$$N$$$, representing the number of hexagonal blocks. The second line contains a string $$$S$$$ of length $$$N$$$, where the $$$i$$$-th character $$$S_i$$$ represents the color of the $$$i$$$-th block from the left, with B representing blue and R representing red.
$$$2 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5$$$
The sum of $$$N$$$ over all games does not exceed $$$2 \times 10^5$$$.
output: Output $$$T$$$ lines, where the $$$i$$$-th line outputs the result of the $$$i$$$-th game. If Doludu wins, output Doludu; otherwise, output DoIudu.

legend: 如果你问Doludu和Doiudu他们最喜欢的形状是什么，他们肯定会说是六边形。因为他们真的太爱六边形了，不管是什么物体，他们总想把它设计成六边形，游戏物品也不例外。
今天，他们要玩一个游戏。在这个游戏中，一开始有$$$N$$$个六边形方块排成一排，这些六边形方块分为蓝色和红色。比赛开始后，他们两人将轮流出招，多鲁杜先出。当轮到玩家时，他必须在当前剩余的方块中移除最左边或最右边的方块。在只剩下一个方块的那一刻，游戏结束。如果这个块是蓝色的，则多鲁杜获胜，否则，多伊乌杜获胜。
Doludu 和 DoIudu 都非常聪明，他们一定会使用最优策略来玩这个游戏。根据 $$$N$$$ 方块的初始颜色，请确定他们中谁会获胜。
input: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$T$$$，表示 Doludu 和 DoIudu 将玩 $$$T$$$ 游戏。
接下来是按顺序排列的每个游戏的细节。单个游戏的信息由两行组成。第一行包含整数$$$N$$$，表示六边形块的数量。第二行包含长度为$$$N$$$的字符串$$$S$$$，其中第$$$i$$$个字符$$$S_i$$$表示从左起第$$$i$$$个块的颜色，B表示蓝色，R表示红色。
所有游戏的 $$$N$$$ 总和不超过 $$$2 \times 10^5$$$。
output: 输出 $$$T$$$ 行，其中 $$$i$$$ 行输出 $$$i$$$ 游戏的结果。如果 Doludu 赢了，输出 Doludu;否则，输出 DoIudu。

problems.hint: In piles.

statement.title: H. Lots of Towers of Hanoi

legend: In the original Towers of Hanoi game, there are three towers of disks. In the initial configuration, all of the disks are on a single tower such that the radii of the disks are sorted in order from smallest to largest, from top to bottom. Here is a picture of the starting position of the original game:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3f8458d4c0a2410ac333ad0d720c0b8fac1ad173.png)

The disks are typically labeled $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, where $$$n$$$ is the number of disks, with $$$1$$$ representing the smallest disk and $$$n$$$ representing the largest disk. In this diagram, the towers are labeled $$$A$$$, $$$B$$$ and $$$C$$$. The goal of the game is to transfer all the disks to a different tower via a sequence of moves. On a single move, one may move the top disk of any tower onto the top disk of another tower, provided that the disk being placed on top is smaller than the disk below it. Alternatively, one may move the top disk of any tower onto an empty tower. To signify a move, it's good enough to simply specify a starting and ending tower. For example, in the above diagram, performing the moves $$$A$$$ to $$$B$$$ followed by $$$A$$$ to $$$C$$$, followed by $$$B$$$ to $$$C$$$ would result in disks $$$3$$$, $$$4$$$, and $$$5$$$ on tower $$$A$$$ and disks $$$1$$$ and $$$2$$$ on tower $$$C$$$.

Luckily, the manufacturers of the game have splurged on the number of towers and have produced a set with $$$k$$$ towers instead of just 3 towers. Due to the generality, the towers are labeled $$$1$$$ through $$$k$$$, instead of $$$A$$$, $$$B$$$ and $$$C$$$. The manufacturers have decided to include $$$n = \frac{k(k-1)}{2}$$$ disks with the set. The directions on the box containing the puzzle claim that the puzzle can be solved with $$$2(k-1)^2$$$ or fewer moves. Write a program to prove the manufacturer's conclusion.

Given the value of $$$k$$$, the number of towers in the Towers of Hanoi game, the number of the starting tower of all the disks, $$$s$$$, and the number of the ending tower of all the disks, $$$e$$$, create a sequence of at most $$$2(k-1)^2$$$ moves that solves the puzzle.
input: The first and only input line contains three integers: $$$k$$$ $$$(3 ≤ k ≤ 1000)$$$, representing the number of towers in the game, $$$s$$$ $$$(1 ≤ s ≤ k)$$$, representing the starting tower for the $$$\frac{k(k-1)}{2}$$$ disks, and $$$e$$$ $$$(1 ≤ e ≤ k, e ≠ s)$$$, representing the ending tower for the $$$\frac{k(k-1)}{2}$$$ disks.
output: The first line of output should contain a single positive integer, $$$m$$$, number of moves in your solution. The following $$$m$$$ lines should contain the contents of each move, in the sequence they are made to solve the puzzle. For each move, simply output two space separated integers, $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ $$$(a ≠ b)$$$, representing the starting and ending towers, respectively, for that particular move.

You do not have to provide the optimal solution; your solution will be accepted as long as it is valid and has $$$2(k-1)^2$$$ or fewer moves.

legend: 在最初的河内塔游戏中，有三座圆盘塔。在最初的配置中，所有圆盘都位于一座塔上，这样圆盘的半径就可以按照从最小到最大、从顶到底的顺序排列。以下是最初游戏的起始位置图：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3f8458d4c0a2410ac333ad0d720c0b8fac1ad173.png)

磁盘通常标记为$$$1$$$到$$$n$$$，其中$$$n$$$是磁盘的数量。其中$$$1$$$表示最小的盘，$$$n$$$表示最大的盘。在该图中，塔被标记为$$$A$$$、$$$B$$$和$$$C$$$。游戏的目标是通过一系列的移动将所有的磁盘转移到不同的塔上。在单次移动中，可以将任何塔的顶部圆盘移动到另一个塔的顶部圆盘上，前提是放置在顶部的磁盘小于其下方的磁盘。或者，可以将任何塔的顶部圆盘移动到空塔上。要表示移动，只需指定开始和结束塔就足够了。例如，在上图中，执行移动$$$A$$$至$$$B$$$，然后执行$$$A$$$至$$$C$$$，然后是$$$B$$$到$$$C$$$，将导致塔$$$A$$$上的磁盘$$$3$$$、$$$4$$$和$$$5$$$以及塔$$$C$$$上的磁盘$$$1$$$和$$$2$$$。

幸运的是，游戏制造商在塔的数量上花了大价钱，制作了一套有 $$$k$$$ 塔的游戏，而不是只有 3 个塔。由于通用性的原因，这些塔被标为 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$k$$$，而不是 $$$A$$$、$$$B$$$ 和 $$$C$$$。生产商决定将$$$n = \frac{k(k-1)}{2}$$$磁盘附在这套谜题中。谜题包装盒上的说明称该谜题可以用$$$2(k-1)^2$$$步或更少的步数解出。请写一个程序来证明制造商的结论。
给定$$$k$$$的值，即《towers of Hanoi》游戏中的塔数，所有磁盘的起始塔数$$$s$$$和所有磁盘的结束塔数$$$e$$$，创建一个最多$$$2(k-1)^2$$$步的序列来解决这个谜题。
output: 第一行输出应包含一个正整数$$$m$$$，即解题过程中的步数。接下来的$$$m$$$行应包含每一步棋的内容，并按照解题顺序排列。对于每一步棋，只需输出两个空格分隔的整数$$$a$$$和$$$b$$$ $$$(a ≠ b)$$$，分别代表该步棋的起点塔和终点塔。
note: 大多数谜题都有许多可能的解决方案。任何有效的解决方案都将被接受。
你不必提供最优解;只要你的解是有效的，并且包含 $$$2(k-1)^2$$$ 或更少的步数，就会被接受。

problems.hint: If $x$ can't be the answer?

legend: You are given an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$. For each $$$k$$$ from $$$2$$$ to $$$n$$$, find the maximum distance between two distinct elements within any subarray of length $$$k$$$.
Formally, for each $$$k$$$, we want to find:
$$$$$$\max \{ j - i \mid 1 \le i  \lt  j \le n, \, j - i  \lt  k, \, a_i \neq a_j \}$$$$$$
If no such pair of distinct elements exists for a given $$$k$$$, the answer is $$$-1$$$.
input: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$, representing the length of the array.
The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$, representing the elements of the array.
$$$2 \le n \le 3 \times 10^5$$$
output: Output $$$n-1$$$ space-separated integers on a single line. The $$$i$$$-th integer should be the answer for $$$k = i + 1$$$.

legend: 给定一个长度为$$$n$$$的数组$$$a$$$。对于$$$2$$$到$$$n$$$中的每个$$$k$$$，求长度为$$$k$$$的任意子数组中两个不同元素之间的最大距离。
$$$$$$\max \{ j - i \mid 1 \le i  \lt  j \le n, \, j - i  \lt  k, \, a_i \neq a_j \}$$$$$$
如果对于给定的$$$k$$$不存在这样的相异元素对，则答案是$$$-1$$$。

problems.hint: Find the connected components in two graphs.

legend: You are given a simple undirected graph $$$G$$$ with $$$n$$$ vertices and $$$m$$$ black edges. The $$$i$$$-th black edge connects vertices $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$. For every pair of distinct vertices not connected by a black edge, there is a white edge between them.
We call two distinct vertices $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ close to gray if both of the following conditions hold:
It is possible to travel from $$$x$$$ to $$$y$$$ using only black edges.
It is possible to travel from $$$x$$$ to $$$y$$$ using only white edges.
Find the number of unordered pairs $$$(x, y)$$$, where $$$1 \leq x  \lt  y \leq n$$$, that are close to gray.
input: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$, representing the number of vertices and black edges, respectively.
Each of the next $$$m$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$, indicating that there is a black edge between them.
$$$2 \leq n \leq 5 \times 10^5$$$
$$$0 \leq m \leq 5 \times 10^5$$$
$$$1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n$$$
$$$u_i \neq v_i$$$
There are no multiple edges between the same pair of vertices.
output: Output a single integer representing the number of unordered pairs that are close to gray.

legend: 给定一个简单的无向图 $$$G$$$，其中包含 $$$n$$$ 顶点和 $$$m$$$ 黑边。$$$i$$$ 第三条黑边连接顶点 $$$u_i$$$ 和 $$$v_i$$$。对于每对不由黑边连接的不同顶点，它们之间都有一条白边。
如果以下两个条件都成立，我们将两个不同的顶点 $$$x$$$ 和 $$$y$$$ 称为接近灰色：
只使用黑边就可以从$$$x$$$移动到$$$y$$$。
可以仅使用白色边缘从 $$$x$$$ 旅行到 $$$y$$$。
找出接近灰色的无序对数 $$$(x, y)$$$，其中 $$$1 \leq x  \lt  y \leq n$$$。
input: 第一行包含两个整数$$$n$$$和$$$m$$$，分别表示顶点数和黑边数。
接下来的 $$$m$$$ 行中的每一行都包含两个整数 $$$u_i$$$ 和 $$$v_i$$$，表明它们之间存在一条黑边。
$$$u_i \neq v_i$$$
在同一对顶点之间没有多条边。
output: 输出单个整数，表示接近灰色的无序对的数量。

problems.hint: If there exists a $x,y,x,y$ subsequence, at least one of $x,y$ should be deleted.

legend: Trida attached $$$n$$$ cables to $$$2n$$$ sockets arranged from left to right. Every cable has a label from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, and its two ends are attached to the two sockets carrying its label.

Two cables are tangled when their ends alternate along the row. In other words, cables $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ are tangled if the four relevant labels appear in the order $$$x,y,x,y$$$ or $$$y,x,y,x$$$, with other labels possibly between them.

Trida will remove exactly one entire cable, including both of its ends. Find all cables she can remove so that no two remaining cables are tangled. If zero or one cable remains after the removal, there is no tangled pair.
input: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5$$$), the number of cables.
The second line contains $$$2n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{2n}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$). Every integer from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ occurs exactly twice.
output: On the first line, print the number $$$k$$$ of cables whose removal leaves no tangled pair.
On the second line, print their $$$k$$$ labels in increasing order. If $$$k=0$$$, print an empty second line.
note: In the sample, removing cable $$$2$$$ leaves the sequence $$$1,1,3,4,4,3$$$, which has no tangled pair. Removing any other cable leaves at least one tangled pair.

legend: Trida 将 $$$n$$$ 电缆连接到从左到右排列的 $$$2n$$$ 插座上。每根电缆都有一个从 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$ 的标签，其两端连接到带有其标签的两个插座上。
Trida 会精确地移除一根完整的电缆，包括其两端。找到所有她能移除的电缆，确保剩下的两根电缆不会纠缠在一起。如果移除后没有剩下零根或一根电缆，则不存在纠缠对。
input: 第一行包含一个整数$$$n$$$($$$1 \le n \le 2 \times 10^5$$$），即电缆数量。
第二行包含$$$2n$$$个整数$$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{2n}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$）。从$$$1$$$到$$$n$$$的每一个整数恰好出现两次。
output: 在第一行打印出移除后没有缠结对的电缆数$$$k$$$。
在第二行，按递增顺序打印它们的$$$k$$$标签。如果$$$k=0$$$，打印空的第二行。

problems.hint: It's about operating on subtrees.

legend: You are given a tree with $$$n$$$ vertices. The score of every vertex is initially $$$0$$$.
You have to process $$$q$$$ queries. Each query contains five integers $$$u$$$, $$$v$$$, $$$x$$$, $$$y$$$, and $$$z$$$. For every vertex $$$r$$$:
add $$$x$$$ to its score if $$$\operatorname{dist}(r,u)  \lt  \operatorname{dist}(r,v)$$$;
add $$$y$$$ to its score if $$$\operatorname{dist}(r,u)  \gt  \operatorname{dist}(r,v)$$$;
add $$$z$$$ to its score if $$$\operatorname{dist}(r,u) = \operatorname{dist}(r,v)$$$.
Here, $$$\operatorname{dist}(a,b)$$$ is the number of edges on the simple path between vertices $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$.
After every query, print the minimum score among all vertices and the number of vertices having this score.
input: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n,q \le 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of vertices and the number of queries.
Each of the next $$$n-1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ ($$$1 \le a,b \le n$$$, $$$a \ne b$$$), denoting an edge between vertices $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$. The given edges form a tree.
Each of the next $$$q$$$ lines contains five integers $$$u$$$, $$$v$$$, $$$x$$$, $$$y$$$, and $$$z$$$ ($$$1 \le u,v \le n$$$, $$$0 \le x,y,z \le 10^9$$$), describing a query.
output: After every query, print two integers: the minimum score among all vertices and the number of vertices having this score.
note: After the first query, the scores of vertices $$$1,2,3,4$$$ are $$$1,4,4,1$$$, respectively. Thus, the minimum score is $$$1$$$, and two vertices have it.
In the last query, $$$u=v=3$$$, so every vertex is equally far from $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. Therefore, $$$z=2$$$ is added to every score.

legend: 给定一棵顶点为 $$$n$$$ 的树，每个顶点的得分最初为 $$$0$$$。
如果是 $$$\operatorname{dist}(r,u)  \lt  \operatorname{dist}(r,v)$$$，则将 $$$x$$$ 添加到其评分中;
如果$$$\operatorname{dist}(r,u)  \gt  \operatorname{dist}(r,v)$$$，则将$$$y$$$添加到其分数
如果是 $$$\operatorname{dist}(r,u) = \operatorname{dist}(r,v)$$$，则将 $$$z$$$ 添加到其评分中。
其中$$$\operatorname{dist}(a,b)$$$为顶点$$$a$$$与$$$b$$$之间的简单路径上的边数。
每次查询后，打印所有顶点的最小得分以及具有该得分的顶点数。
input: 第一行包含两个整数$$$n$$$和$$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n,q \le 2\cdot 10^5$$$）——顶点的数量和查询的数量。
接下来的每一行 $$$n-1$$$ 都包含两个整数 $$$a$$$ 和 $$$b$$$($$$1 \le a,b \le n$$$,$$$a \ne b$$$)，表示顶点 $$$a$$$ 和 $$$b$$$ 之间的边。给定的边形成一棵树。
note: 在最后一个查询中，$$$u=v=3$$$，因此每个顶点距离 $$$u$$$ 和 $$$v$$$ 的距离相等。因此，$$$z=2$$$ 被添加到每个评分中。

problems.hint: How can you decide the cost of an array? And you can decide the elements one by one.

legend: $$$\text{WisdomCasual}$$$ was supposed to prepare this problem for the $$$\text{UEPC}$$$ a week ago. Naturally, he forgot.

With only 30 minutes left before $$$\text{cgmoreda}$$$'s deadline, he scribbled down an idea involving arrays and operations. He thinks it is brilliant, but he has no time to solve it or assess its difficulty. He needs you to solve it for him and tell him the difficulty.
Here is the problem he wrote down:
You are given three integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$, and $$$x$$$. You need to construct an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ integers that satisfies the following conditions:
$$$-k \le a_i \le k$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$.
The sum of all elements in the array is exactly $$$0$$$: $$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i = 0$$$.
The cost of the array is at most $$$x$$$.
The cost of an array is defined as the minimum number of operations required to make all elements in the array equal to $$$0$$$.
In one operation, you can choose an index $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \le i  \lt  n$$$) and do exactly one of the following:
Decrease $$$a_i$$$ by $$$1$$$ and increase $$$a_{i+1}$$$ by $$$1$$$.
Increase $$$a_i$$$ by $$$1$$$ and decrease $$$a_{i+1}$$$ by $$$1$$$.

Since $$$\text{WisdomCasual}$$$ wants to ensure the problem has a unique output, you must find the lexicographically smallest array $$$a$$$ that satisfies all the above conditions. (He doesn't have enough time to write a custom checker)
Can you solve it for him and save his deadline?

Note: An array $$$a$$$ is lexicographically smaller than an array $$$b$$$ of the same length if, at the first index where they differ, the element in $$$a$$$ is strictly smaller than the corresponding element in $$$b$$$.
input: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$)  — the number of test cases.
The only line of each test case contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$, and $$$x$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le k \le 10^9$$$, $$$0 \le x \le 10^{18}$$$).
It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, output $$$n$$$ integers representing the lexicographically smallest valid array $$$a$$$.
It is guaranteed that under the given constraints, at least one valid array always exists.

legend: $$$\text{WisdomCasual}$$$应在一周前为$$$\text{UEPC}$$$准备此问题。自然，他忘了。
在距离 $$$\text{cgmoreda}$$$ 的最后期限只剩下 30 分钟的时候，他草草写下了一个涉及阵列和操作的想法。他认为这个想法很棒，但他没有时间解决它或评估它的难度。他需要你帮他解决它，并告诉他难度。
下面是他写下的问题：
给定三个整数 $$$n$$$、$$$k$$$ 和 $$$x$$$。需要构造一个满足以下条件的 $$$n$$$ 整数数组 $$$a$$$:
$$$-k \le a_i \le k$$$适用于所有$$$1 \le i \le n$$$。
数组中所有元素的和正好是$$$0$$$: $$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i = 0$$$。
数组的开销定义为使数组中所有元素等于 $$$0$$$ 所需的最小操作数。
在一次操作中，您可以选择索引$$$i$$$ ($$$1 \le i  \lt  n$$$）并执行以下操作之一：
由于$$$\text{WisdomCasual}$$$想要确保问题有唯一的输出，您必须找到字典顺序上最小的数组$$$a$$$，它满足上述所有条件。(他没有足够的时间编写自定义检查器）
注意：数组$$$a$$$在字典序上小于相同长度的数组$$$b$$$，如果在它们不同的第一个索引处，$$$a$$$中的元素严格小于$$$b$$$中的相应元素。
input: 第一行包含一个整数 $$$t$$$($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$)——测试用例的数量。
保证所有测试用例的$$$n$$$总和不超过$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$。
output: 对于每个测试用例，输出 $$$n$$$ 整数表示词典编纂学中最小的有效数组 $$$a$$$。

legend: After another long BedWars session, Muzan and Honey decided to create a highlights video from their match.
They have $$$N$$$ recorded clips, each represented by a string of lowercase English letters.
First, Honey must arrange the clips in any order, using every clip exactly once, and concatenate them into one long replay $$$T$$$.

Before uploading it, Muzan suggests starting the replay from a different moment. For an integer $$$k$$$ with $$$0 \le k  \lt  |T|$$$, a cyclic shift by $$$k$$$ characters moves the first $$$k$$$ characters of $$$T$$$ to the end. They may choose any such $$$k$$$ to obtain a new replay $$$T'$$$.
For example, if $$$T = \texttt{abcde}$$$, its possible cyclic shifts are:
They are looking for a famous BedWars combo, represented by the string $$$P$$$.
Choose both the order of the clips and the cyclic shift so that the number of linear occurrences of $$$P$$$ as a substring of $$$T'$$$ is maximized. Occurrences are allowed to overlap.

Rotating $$$\texttt{baab}$$$ by two characters gives $$$\texttt{abba}$$$, which contains the target exactly once. Therefore, the answer is $$$1$$$.

legend: It is 5 AM, and $$$WisdomCasual$$$ is exhausted. He has been setting problems all night, and all he wants to do right now is get into bed and sleep. However, the problemset is still missing a problem.
In a desperate attempt to finish the problem and finally get some rest, he quickly writes down two arrays, $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, both of size $$$n$$$, and writes a random condition on a napkin.

$$$1 \le i  \lt  j \le n$$$

The absolute difference between the elements in array $$$a$$$ is exactly equal to the absolute difference between the corresponding elements in array $$$b$$$. Formally: $$$\vert{}a_i - a_j\vert{} = \vert{}b_i - b_j\vert{}$$$

Since $$$WisdomCasual$$$ is already half-asleep, he leaves the task of actually counting the pairs to you. Help him find the total number of synchronized pairs so he can finally close his eyes and go to sleep...

It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the total number of synchronized pairs.

legend: You are given a binary grid $$$a$$$ with $$$n$$$ rows and $$$m$$$ columns.

Three cells form an angle if they can be written as $$$(i,j)$$$, $$$(i,y)$$$, and $$$(x,j)$$$, where $$$x \ne i$$$ and $$$y \ne j$$$, and all three cells contain $$$1$$$. The cell $$$(i,j)$$$ is the corner of the angle.
You must choose exactly one cell containing $$$0$$$ and change it to $$$1$$$.
Find the maximum possible number of angles after the change, and the number of cells whose change gives this maximum.
It is guaranteed that the grid contains at least one $$$0$$$.
input: The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n \cdot m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, print two integers: the maximum possible number of angles and the number of cells whose change gives this maximum.
note: In the first test case, either zero creates one angle. In the second, changing the only zero makes each of the four cells the corner of an angle. In the fourth, any cell in the second row creates two angles. In the fifth, a one-row grid cannot contain an angle, so either zero is optimal.

legend: You are given three integers $$$x, y, z$$$ and a string $$$S$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ lowercase English letters.

legend: $$$Da7doo7$$$ believed he had mastered competitive programming contests, so he decided to turn his attention to playing basketball.
$$$Da7doo7$$$ intends to shoot $$$n$$$ balls into the basket. The probability of him scoring the first shot is $$$\frac{p_0}{q_0}$$$.
For subsequent shots, his probability of scoring depends on whether he made the previous shot or not:
If he scored shot $$$i-1$$$, the probability of scoring shot $$$i$$$ is $$$\frac{p_1}{q_1}$$$.
If he missed shot $$$i-1$$$, the probability of scoring shot $$$i$$$ is $$$\frac{p_2}{q_2}$$$.
$$$Da7doo7$$$ is asking for your help to find the expected value of the number of balls that will score.

We can show that the answer can be written in the form $$$\frac{P}{Q}$$$ where $$$P, Q$$$ are coprime integers and $$$Q \neq 0 \bmod 998244353$$$. Output the value of $$$(P \cdot Q^{-1})$$$ modulo $$$998244353$$$.

legend: $n$ wizards stood in a circle and decided to perform $q$ rituals.

We number the wizards from $1$ to $n$ in a clockwise direction. The $i$-th ritual involves wizard number $k$ if there exists a non-negative integer $x$ such that $(\mathit{first}_i + \mathit{step}_i \cdot x - 1) \bmod n + 1 = k$, where mod is the modulus operation. For better understanding, it is worth looking at the illustration in the example.

Initially, each wizard had $10^{18}$ units of mana. The $i$-th ritual changes the mana of the involved wizards by $\mathit{cost}_i$. That is, if $\mathit{cost}_i > 0$, the mana increases by $|\mathit{cost}_i|$ units; if $\mathit{cost}_i < 0$, it decreases by $|\mathit{cost}_i|$ units; and if $\mathit{cost}_i = 0$, it remains unchanged.
Determine the number of the wizard with the most mana after all $q$ rituals. If there are several, choose the one with the smallest number.
**Scoring**
The tests for this problem consist of ten groups. Points for each group are awarded only if all tests of the group and all tests of the required groups are passed.

- Group 1 (10 points): $n, q \le 5000$; $n$ is a multiple of $\mathit{step}_i$ for all $i$; no required groups
- Group 2 (10 points): $n, q \le 5000$; $\mathit{step}_i \le n$ for all $i$; requires group 1
- Group 3 (10 points): $n, q \le 5000$; requires groups 1, 2
- Group 4 (10 points): $\mathit{first}_i = \mathit{first}_j$ for all $i, j$; $n$ is a multiple of $\mathit{step}_i$ for all $i$; no required groups
- Group 5 (10 points): $\mathit{step}_i = \mathit{step}_j$ for all $i, j$; $n$ is a multiple of $\mathit{step}_i$ for all $i$; no required groups
- Group 6 (10 points): $n$ is a multiple of $\mathit{step}_i$ for all $i$; requires groups 1, 4, 5
- Group 7 (10 points): $\mathit{first}_i = \mathit{first}_j$ for all $i, j$; $\mathit{step}_i \le n$ for all $i$; requires group 4
- Group 8 (10 points): $\mathit{step}_i = \mathit{step}_j$ for all $i, j$; $\mathit{step}_i \le n$ for all $i$; requires group 5
- Group 9 (10 points): $\mathit{step}_i \le n$ for all $i$; requires groups 1, 2, 4–8
- Group 10 (10 points): no additional constraints; requires groups 1–9
input: The first line contains two integers $n$ and $q$ ($1 \le n, q \le 2 \cdot 10^5$).

In the $i$-th of the following $q$ lines, there are 3 integers $\mathit{first}_i$, $\mathit{step}_i$, and $\mathit{cost}_i$ ($1 \le \mathit{first}_i \le n$; $1 \le \mathit{step}_i \le 10^9$; $-10^9 \le \mathit{cost}_i \le 10^9$).

legend: $n$巫师们围成一圈，决定举行$q$仪式。
我们在顺时针方向上给巫师编号从 $1$ 到 $n$。如果存在一个非负整数 $x$，使得 $(\mathit{first}_i + \mathit{step}_i \cdot x - 1) \bmod n + 1 = k$，其中 mod 是模运算，则 $i$ 第一个仪式涉及巫师编号 $k$。为了更好地理解，值得参考示例中的示例。
最初，每个巫师有$10^{18}$单位的法力。$i$-仪式改变了$\mathit{cost}_i$法师的法力。也就是说，如果$\mathit{cost}_i > 0$，魔法值增加$|\mathit{cost}_i|$个单位；如果$\mathit{cost}_i < 0$，则减少$|\mathit{cost}_i|$个单位；如果$\mathit{cost}_i = 0$，它保持不变。

statement.title: E. Jamal Fofo Two of a Kind Length of a Path Out of Your Mind

legend: It is a well-known fact in the problemsetting room: Fofo absolutely despises trees, and Jamal harbors an intense hatred for grids. Naturally, the room was left in stunned silence when Fofo, with a mischievous grin, unexpectedly proposed a tree problem.
Before the ink could even dry, Jamal narrowed his eyes and hit him with a swift, merciless $$$\texttt{3rr}$$$.
"Project it onto a grid," Jamal demanded.
After a fierce clash of wills, a compromise was born. What lies before you is the ultimate cocktail of Jamal and Fofo's $$$\texttt{7as7aseh}$$$—a grid problem haunted by the ghost of a tree.

Consider an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. A path is a sequence of cells moving exclusively down or to the right, starting and ending at distinct positions. The length of a path is the total number of cells it traverses.

Your challenge is to survive their $$$\texttt{7as7aseh}$$$ by filling the grid with positive integers such that it satisfies one core property: for every path of length $$$L$$$, at least two cells along that path must contain values divisible by $$$L$$$.
If their combined trap is too strong and no such valid grid exists, report that it is impossible.
input: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.
Each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n,m \le 300$$$) — the number of rows and columns.
It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n \cdot m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$90000$$$.
output: For each test case, print NO if it is impossible to construct a valid grid.
Otherwise, print YES, followed by $$$n$$$ lines. Each of these lines must contain $$$m$$$ integers, the values in the grid. Every value must be between $$$1$$$ and $$$10^9$$$, inclusive.
You may print YES and NO in any case. If there are several valid grids, print any of them.
note: The provided sample illustrates just one possible valid configuration.
In the first test case, there does not exist any path starting and ending at distinct positions. Hence, any grid works.

titleZh: E.贾马尔·佛佛两个人的一种长度的一条小路走出了你的脑海。

legend: 墨迹还没干，贾马尔就眯起眼睛，用一个迅速而无情的 $$$\texttt{3rr}$$$ 击中了他。

考虑$$$n \times m$$$网格。路径是专门向下或向右移动的单元格序列，在不同的位置开始和结束。路径的长度是它所遍历的单元格的总数。
你的挑战是通过用正整数填充网格来生存$$$\texttt{7as7aseh}$$$，使其满足一个核心属性：对于长度为$$$L$$$的每条路径，该路径上至少有两个单元格必须包含可被$$$L$$$整除的值。
如果它们的组合陷阱过于强大，且不存在这样的有效网格，请报告这是不可能的。
